subServices.name: Breakdown & Won't-Start Callouts
subServices.blurb: Car dead in a Townsville driveway, work carpark or shopping centre? Get connected with mobile mechanics who diagnose and, where possible, fix it where it sits - no tow needed.
subServices.whatItInvolves: A won't-start callout is the job mobile mechanics are built for, because the one thing a dead car cannot do is drive to a workshop. The mechanic comes to the vehicle with a scan tool, a multimeter and a battery tester, and works through the short list of causes in order: battery state of charge and cranking amps, terminal corrosion, starter motor and solenoid, alternator output, fuses and relays, then fuel delivery and immobiliser faults. In Townsville a large share of these calls end at the battery, because sustained tropical heat cooks electrolyte and shortens battery life well below the four-to-five years a car battery manages in a cooler climate. Many faults are repairable on the spot - a battery, a terminal, a relay, a fuse. Where the fault is internal to the engine or transmission, the value of the callout is a diagnosis you can act on and a written fault report, so you are not paying to tow a car to a workshop before anyone knows what is wrong with it.
whenYouNeedIt: The car cranks but will not fire, or clicks once and does nothing, in your own driveway
Dashboard warning lights came on and the engine cut out on the Bruce Highway or Ross River Road
The car will not start in a work carpark at Lavarack Barracks, the port, or a Kirwan or Aitkenvale shopping centre
Headlights and dash are dim or dead after the car sat through a hot week unused
You want a diagnosis before deciding whether the car is worth towing anywhere

process.detail: Whether it cranks, clicks or is completely dead narrows the likely cause before anyone leaves - and tells the mechanic which parts to carry.
Battery voltage under load, cranking amps, alternator charge rate and earth connections are tested first, because that is where most no-start faults end.
If the electrics test clean, a scan tool pulls stored fault codes and the mechanic works through starter, fuel and immobiliser circuits.
Batteries, terminals, fuses and relays are usually replaced in the same visit. Internal engine faults get a written diagnosis so you can decide the next step.

subServices.priceGuide: Mobile call-out fees across Australia generally run $50-$100 to cover travel and initial diagnosis, with labour typically $80-$150 per hour on top. A no-start that turns out to be the battery is often the cheapest possible outcome - one visit, one part, no tow truck. After-hours and weekend callouts attract a premium. Get a couple of quotes and confirm whether the call-out fee is credited against the repair.

faqs.question: Can a mobile mechanic fix a car that won't start at all?
faqs.answer: In most cases yes. The common causes of a no-start - a flat or failed battery, corroded terminals, a blown fuse, a faulty relay or a dead starter solenoid - are all repairable at the roadside with parts carried on the van. Faults inside the engine or transmission cannot be fixed in a driveway, but the diagnosis still saves you towing a car somewhere before anyone knows what is wrong.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper than towing the car to a workshop?
faqs.answer: Usually, when the fault is electrical. A tow plus a workshop diagnostic charge often exceeds a mobile call-out fee and an on-site battery replacement. Where the car does need workshop equipment, you have at least paid for a diagnosis rather than a blind tow.

subServices.name: Warranty-Safe Logbook Servicing
subServices.blurb: Scheduled logbook servicing done in your driveway or work carpark. Under Australian Consumer Law a qualified independent mechanic can stamp your logbook without voiding a new-car warranty.
subServices.whatItInvolves: A logbook service follows the manufacturer's schedule for your specific vehicle at that specific interval - not a generic oil change. Depending on where the car sits in its schedule that means engine oil and filter, air and cabin filters, spark plugs, brake fluid, coolant condition, transmission and differential oils, belt and hose inspection, brake and tyre wear measurement, suspension and steering check, and a road test. The mechanic then signs and stamps the relevant logbook page. The point that stops most people booking an independent is the warranty question, and the ACCC has been explicit about it: under Australian Consumer Law you are not required to service at an authorised dealer to keep your manufacturer warranty, provided the work is done by appropriately qualified staff, to the manufacturer's specifications and intervals, using parts suitable for the vehicle. They do not have to be genuine manufacturer parts. Done mobile, the service happens while the car is parked at home or at work, which removes the drop-off and pick-up entirely.
whenYouNeedIt: Your logbook interval is due and you do not want to lose a day to a dealer drop-off
A dealer has quoted well above what the same scheduled service costs elsewhere
You work shifts and cannot get a car to a workshop during business hours
You are selling the car and want the service history complete and stamped
The car is a work vehicle that cannot be off the road for a full day

process.detail: The mechanic checks your logbook and odometer against the manufacturer schedule so the right service is quoted - a 40,000km service is a very different job to a 10,000km one.
Because the schedule is known in advance, a logbook service can be quoted accurately up front, including the specific oil and filters your vehicle takes.
Fluids, filters and scheduled checks are completed where the car is parked, with used oil and filters taken away for disposal.
The logbook page is signed and stamped and you get a report on anything found - brake and tyre wear, leaks, or items due at the next interval.

subServices.priceGuide: Mobile logbook servicing in Australia generally runs $180-$500 depending on the vehicle and which interval is due, with a basic oil and filter change typically $80-$180. European vehicles, longer intervals and services that include spark plugs or transmission fluid sit at the top of that range. Ask for the quote to be itemised into parts and labour so you can compare it against a dealer quote line for line.

faqs.question: Will an independent mobile mechanic void my new car warranty?
faqs.answer: No. The ACCC has confirmed that under Australian Consumer Law you can have your vehicle serviced by an independent repairer and keep your manufacturer's warranty, as long as the mechanic is appropriately qualified, follows the manufacturer's specifications and service intervals, and uses parts suitable for the vehicle. Parts do not have to be genuine branded parts. If a dealer refuses warranty coverage purely because you used an independent, the ACCC can be contacted on 1300 302 502.

faqs.question: Can a mobile mechanic stamp the logbook even though it says authorised dealer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Even where the logbook page is labelled for an authorised dealer, an independent repairer can sign and stamp it, and the logbook and warranty remain valid provided the scheduled work was carried out to specification.

subServices.name: Mobile Car Battery Testing & Replacement
subServices.blurb: Townsville's heat is hard on batteries. Get connected with mobile mechanics who test the battery and charging system on site and fit a correctly rated replacement where the car is parked.
subServices.whatItInvolves: Battery work is the single most common mobile mechanic job in a tropical city, and the reason is chemistry rather than bad luck. Sustained high temperatures accelerate the internal reactions in a lead-acid battery, evaporate electrolyte and corrode the plates and terminals, and constant air-conditioning load adds electrical strain on top. Batteries that would last four to five years in a temperate climate routinely fall short of that in the north. A proper job is not just swapping the box. The mechanic load-tests the existing battery to confirm it has actually failed, then tests alternator output and the charging circuit - because a battery that died early often died because the alternator was undercharging or a parasitic drain was flattening it overnight. Replacing the battery without finding that fault buys you a few months and the same problem. The replacement is matched on physical size, terminal layout and cold cranking amps, and on modern vehicles with stop-start systems it must be the correct AGM or EFB type, with the battery registered to the car's charging management system.
whenYouNeedIt: The engine cranks slowly or the starter clicks, especially first thing in the morning
Headlights and interior lights dim noticeably when you turn the key
The battery is more than three years old and has spent those years in Townsville heat
You have needed a jump-start more than once in a fortnight
The car sat unused for a couple of weeks and will no longer start

process.detail: Voltage alone does not prove a battery is good. A load test measures whether it still delivers its rated cranking amps under real draw.
Alternator output and any parasitic drain are checked, so an early failure is traced to its cause rather than repeated in six months.
Size, terminal position, cold cranking amps and type are matched to the vehicle - AGM or EFB where a stop-start system requires it.
The new battery is fitted, registered to the charging system where the vehicle needs it, terminals are cleaned and protected, and the old battery is taken away for recycling.

subServices.priceGuide: Expect the battery itself to be the bulk of the cost, with the mobile call-out fee typically $50-$100 on top. AGM and EFB batteries for stop-start vehicles cost noticeably more than a standard flooded battery, and larger diesel and 4WD batteries more again. Ask what warranty comes with the battery and whether the charging system test is included - a replacement fitted without that test is the one most likely to fail early.

faqs.question: Why do car batteries fail faster in Townsville?
faqs.answer: Heat is the main driver. High ambient temperatures speed up the internal chemical reactions in a lead-acid battery, cause electrolyte loss and increase corrosion at the plates and terminals, all of which reduce capacity. Heavy air-conditioning use adds further electrical load. Batteries in consistently hot climates commonly fall well short of the four to five years typical elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can the battery be replaced without me being there?
faqs.answer: Often yes, provided the vehicle is accessible and unlocked or keys are arranged, which is why a lot of these jobs are done in work carparks during a shift. Confirm access arrangements when booking - some modern vehicles need the ignition and the battery registration step completed, which requires the key on site.

subServices.name: Brake Repairs & Pad Replacement
subServices.blurb: Grinding, squealing or a spongy pedal? Connect with mobile mechanics who measure pad and rotor wear at your address and replace pads and discs on site.
subServices.whatItInvolves: Brake work is well suited to mobile service because it needs hand tools and jack stands rather than a hoist. The mechanic removes the wheels, measures remaining pad thickness against the manufacturer's minimum, checks the discs for thickness, scoring, lipping and heat cracking, inspects calliper slides and pistons for seizure, and checks the flexible hoses and brake fluid condition. Pads and, where needed, discs are replaced, calliper slides are cleaned and lubricated, and the brakes are bedded in on a short road test. Fluid is checked for moisture content, since brake fluid absorbs water over time and that lowers its boiling point - which is what produces a soft pedal after sustained braking. On the Townsville run down from Hervey Range or Mount Stuart, that matters more than it does on flat suburban driving. Machining badly scored rotors generally requires a lathe, so a mobile job will usually replace discs rather than machine them.
whenYouNeedIt: A squeal or metallic grinding noise when braking
The brake pedal feels soft, spongy or travels further than it used to
The car pulls to one side under braking, or the steering wheel shudders
A brake wear warning light has appeared on the dash
A service or safety inspection has flagged pads or discs as near minimum

process.detail: Wheels come off and pad and disc thickness are measured against the manufacturer minimum, so you replace what is actually worn.
Calliper slides, pistons, flexible hoses and fluid condition are checked - a seized slide is what wears one pad out three times as fast as its partner.
Pads and, where required, discs are fitted, with slides cleaned and greased so the new pads wear evenly.
New pads are bedded in on a short road test to seat the friction material and confirm pedal feel before the mechanic leaves.

subServices.priceGuide: Brake jobs are usually quoted per axle. Pads alone are the cheaper end; pads and discs together roughly double it, and larger 4WD and European brakes cost more again. Mobile labour typically runs $80-$150 per hour plus the call-out fee. Ask whether the quote includes discs or pads only, and whether brake fluid is being replaced - a quote that looks unusually low often covers pads on worn discs, which wears the new pads out early.

faqs.question: Can brakes safely be done in a driveway?
faqs.answer: Yes, on a level solid surface with the vehicle properly supported on jack stands - it is standard mobile mechanic work requiring hand tools rather than a hoist. What generally cannot be done mobile is machining scored rotors, which needs a workshop lathe, so a mobile job will usually replace discs instead.

faqs.question: How do I know if I need discs as well as pads?
faqs.answer: Discs are replaced when they are below minimum thickness, deeply scored, cracked or warped enough to cause shudder. The mechanic measures thickness rather than eyeballing it. Fitting new pads onto discs that are past minimum is a false economy, because the uneven surface chews the new pads out quickly.

subServices.name: Pre-Purchase Vehicle Inspections
subServices.blurb: Buying privately in Townsville? Get connected with mobile mechanics who inspect the car at the seller's address and give you a written report before you hand over money.
subServices.whatItInvolves: A pre-purchase inspection is a mobile mechanic's most valuable job per dollar, because it is the one that stops you buying someone else's problem. The mechanic travels to wherever the car is - a private seller's driveway, a dealer yard - and works through a structured inspection: body and panel alignment for signs of accident repair, rust in the usual traps, chassis and underbody condition, engine and transmission operation, oil and coolant condition and any cross-contamination, a scan for stored and pending fault codes including ones that have been recently cleared, brakes, steering, suspension, tyres including date codes and uneven wear, and a road test for noises, gear changes and braking behaviour. In coastal North Queensland, underbody and cavity corrosion deserves particular attention - salt air and humidity attack vehicles here faster than in inland or southern markets, and a car that spent its life near the beach can look immaculate on top. You get a written report with photos, which is also useful leverage on price.
whenYouNeedIt: Buying privately from a seller you do not know
The car has come from interstate and you cannot see its service history in person
The seller is pushing for a fast cash sale or resisting an inspection
The vehicle has spent its life near the coast and you want the underbody checked for corrosion
You want an independent report before negotiating on price

process.detail: The inspection happens where the vehicle is, so the seller is not asked to drive it anywhere - which also means you see it in its normal state.
Body, underbody, engine, transmission, brakes, steering, suspension and tyres are worked through against a checklist rather than a quick look.
A scan tool pulls stored and pending fault codes, including evidence of recently cleared ones, and a road test checks how it actually drives.
You get a written report with photos covering faults found, what they will cost to put right, and anything that should stop the sale.

subServices.priceGuide: Pre-purchase inspections are typically a flat fee rather than an hourly rate, and sit in a similar range to a basic service. Set against the cost of a failed transmission or hidden accident damage, it is the cheapest insurance in a private sale. Confirm up front whether the fee includes a written report with photos and a scan-tool check, since a visual-only inspection misses cleared fault codes.

faqs.question: Is a pre-purchase inspection the same as a Queensland safety certificate?
faqs.answer: No. A safety certificate is a legal roadworthiness document that in Queensland must be issued by an Approved Inspection Station, and it checks a defined minimum safety standard. A pre-purchase inspection is a far broader commercial assessment of the vehicle's mechanical condition, service history and likely upcoming costs. A car can hold a valid safety certificate and still be a poor buy.

faqs.question: What should I be most worried about on a North Queensland car?
faqs.answer: Corrosion. Salt air and high humidity attack underbody panels, chassis rails, suspension mounts and body cavities faster here than in inland or southern markets, and it is frequently invisible from a walk-around. A proper inspection gets the car up and looks underneath.

faqs.question: How much does a mobile mechanic cost in Townsville?
faqs.answer: Mobile mechanics across Australia typically charge a call-out fee of $50-$100 to cover travel and initial diagnosis, plus labour generally in the $80-$150 per hour range, with parts on top. A completed job commonly lands around $180-$220, a logbook service $180-$500 depending on the vehicle, and a basic oil and filter change $80-$180. There are no fixed industry rates, so pricing varies with urgency, day of the week and job complexity - which is exactly why comparing a few local quotes is worth the ten minutes.

faqs.question: Will servicing with a mobile mechanic void my new car warranty?
faqs.answer: No. The ACCC has confirmed that under Australian Consumer Law you are not required to service at an authorised dealer to keep your manufacturer warranty. An independent mechanic can carry out and stamp your logbook service, provided they are appropriately qualified, follow the manufacturer's specifications and service intervals, and use parts suitable for the vehicle - the parts do not need to be genuine branded parts.

faqs.question: What can't be done in my driveway?
faqs.answer: Most servicing, brake work, batteries, alternators, starters, cooling system work, suspension components and diagnostics are routine mobile jobs. What needs a workshop is anything requiring a hoist, a machining lathe or specialised equipment - internal engine and transmission rebuilds, clutch replacement on many vehicles, wheel alignments and rotor machining. A mobile mechanic can still diagnose those on site so you know what you are dealing with before committing to a tow.

faqs.question: Is this a mechanical workshop?
faqs.answer: No. This site is a free quote-matching service for Townsville drivers. We are not a mechanic and we do not carry out repairs, quote prices ourselves or hold an Approved Inspection Station licence. You tell us what the car is doing and we connect you with local mobile mechanics who quote directly. Always confirm a mechanic's qualifications, insurance and quoted price with them before work starts.

Phase 0 fit is good - emergency electrical is a listed preferred niche and job value clears $500+ on switchboard upgrades, rewires and emergency callouts. Second Ballarat site (ballaratrestumping is live) - different niche, no interlinking, separate GSC property.

subServices.name: Emergency Electrician Callouts
subServices.blurb: Power out, a breaker that will not reset, or a burning smell from the switchboard? Get connected with Ballarat electricians available for urgent same-day and after-hours callouts.
subServices.whatItInvolves: An emergency callout starts with isolating the hazard and then finding the fault, which is rarely where the symptom appears. The electrician confirms whether the outage is on your side of the meter or the network's, then works through the switchboard: which circuit has tripped, whether it is an overload, a short, or an earth leakage fault picked up by an RCD. From there the fault is traced along the circuit - damaged cabling, a failed appliance drawing leakage current, water ingress into an outdoor outlet or a rodent-damaged run in a roof space. A burning smell or scorching at the board is treated as urgent regardless of whether power is still on, because it usually means a loose connection arcing under load, and arcing at a switchboard is a fire risk. In Ballarat's older housing stock, a repeat-tripping circuit frequently traces back to rubber or VIR-insulated wiring that has gone brittle with age. Any installation work carried out must be accompanied by a Certificate of Electrical Safety.
whenYouNeedIt: A circuit breaker or safety switch trips immediately every time you reset it
Burning smell, scorch marks, buzzing or heat at the switchboard or a power point
Part of the house has lost power while the neighbours still have theirs
Water has got into outdoor lighting, a shed circuit or a power point
Sparks, arcing or a shock from an appliance, switch or outlet

process.detail: The affected circuit is isolated at the board before any diagnosis begins - particularly where there is heat, scorching or water involved.
The electrician confirms whether the problem is inside your installation or upstream on the distribution network, which decides who fixes it.
Insulation resistance and earth leakage testing narrows the fault to a section of cabling, an accessory or a specific appliance rather than replacing parts on guesswork.
The fault is repaired, the circuit tested, and a Certificate of Electrical Safety issued for the installation work as Victorian law requires.

subServices.priceGuide: Victorian electricians typically charge $85-$130 per hour for standard residential work, with a first-hour call-out fee generally $80-$150 that usually covers travel plus 30-60 minutes on site. Emergency and after-hours callouts push rates to roughly $150-$250+ per hour. Ask up front what the call-out covers, whether after-hours rates apply at the time you are calling, and whether a minimum charge applies.

faqs.question: My safety switch keeps tripping - is that an emergency?
faqs.answer: A safety switch that trips once and resets cleanly is often a single faulty appliance; unplug things one at a time and retest. A switch that trips instantly every time you reset it, or one accompanied by any burning smell, heat or scorching at the board, needs an electrician promptly. The RCD is doing its job by detecting current leaking to earth, and that leakage path is a genuine shock risk.

faqs.question: Who fixes it if the power is out on my street too?
faqs.answer: If neighbouring properties have lost supply as well, the fault is on the distribution network and the network operator restores it - an electrician cannot. If your property alone is out, the fault is inside your installation and that is an electrician's job. Checking whether the neighbours have power before you call is the fastest way to avoid paying a call-out fee for a network outage.

subServices.name: Switchboard Upgrades & Safety Switches
subServices.blurb: Replacing an old ceramic fuse or rewireable board with modern circuit breakers and RCDs. Compare quotes from Registered Electrical Contractors in Ballarat.
subServices.whatItInvolves: A switchboard upgrade replaces an obsolete board - ceramic rewireable fuses, or early plastic boards with no residual current protection - with a modern enclosure carrying circuit breakers (MCBs) and residual current devices. The distinction matters: a fuse or circuit breaker protects the wiring from overload and fire, while an RCD protects a person from electrocution by cutting power within milliseconds when it detects current leaking to earth. An old fuse board does the first job and none of the second. The work involves fitting the new enclosure, transferring and reterminating every circuit onto appropriately rated breakers, installing two or more RCDs split across circuit groups so one fault does not black out the whole house, labelling every circuit, and testing. Older Ballarat homes often turn up surprises once the board is open - undersized mains, degraded consumer mains, or aged circuit wiring that will not pass insulation testing - so a good quote allows for inspection before committing. Switchboard work is prescribed electrical installation work in Victoria, which means an independent Licensed Electrical Inspector must inspect and countersign the certificate.
whenYouNeedIt: The board still uses ceramic fuses with rewireable fuse wire
There are no safety switches, or only one covering a couple of circuits
Breakers trip as soon as the heating, oven and kettle run together
You are adding solar, an EV charger, ducted heating or a major renovation load
The property is rented - Victorian rentals have required modern switchboards with circuit breakers and RCDs since 29 March 2023

process.detail: The electrician opens the existing board to check consumer mains size, earthing and circuit condition - the things that turn a simple swap into a bigger job.
Circuits are grouped across two or more RCDs so a single fault does not take out the whole house, with dedicated breakers for high-load circuits.
New enclosure fitted, every circuit reterminated onto correctly rated breakers, and every circuit clearly labelled.
Testing includes tripping each RCD under load. As prescribed work, an independent Licensed Electrical Inspector inspects and countersigns the Certificate of Electrical Safety.

subServices.priceGuide: Switchboard upgrades in Victoria generally run $735-$2,950, with a standard three-bedroom home taking around three to four hours and covering the new enclosure, circuit breakers, two or more RCDs, labelling and testing. Because it is prescribed work, budget a further $150-$300 for the independent inspection. Costs climb where consumer mains need upgrading or aged circuit wiring fails insulation testing - which is why quotes given without opening the board are worth treating carefully.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a circuit breaker and a safety switch?
faqs.answer: They protect different things. A circuit breaker (or fuse) protects the wiring by cutting power when the circuit is overloaded or shorted - it prevents fires. A safety switch, or RCD, protects people by detecting current leaking to earth, such as through someone touching a live part, and cutting supply within milliseconds. An old fuse board gives you the first and none of the second, which is the core reason to upgrade.

faqs.question: Does a switchboard upgrade need an inspection in Victoria?
faqs.answer: Yes. Switchboard work falls under prescribed electrical installation work, which under the Electricity Safety Act 1998 must be inspected by a Licensed Electrical Inspector working independently of the contractor. The inspector countersigns the Certificate of Electrical Safety after testing. That inspection fee is a separate cost, so check whether a quote includes it.

subServices.name: Rental Electrical Safety Checks
subServices.blurb: Victorian rental providers must have switchboards, wiring and fittings checked every two years by a licensed electrician. From 13 October 2026 it applies to every rental agreement, new or existing.
subServices.whatItInvolves: This is a defined compliance inspection, not a general look-around. A licensed electrician assesses the installation in accordance with section 4 of AS/NZS 3019:2022 'Electrical installations - Periodic assessment', covering the switchboard, fixed wiring, power points, hardwired light fittings and every installed safety switch. The critical detail, and the one that separates a real check from a cursory one, is that each RCD must be tested under load to confirm it actually trips within the required response time - a visual confirmation that an RCD is present is explicitly not sufficient. Since 29 March 2023, Victorian rental properties have also been required to have a modern-style switchboard with circuit breakers and RCDs installed, so an older board found during the check is a compliance failure that has to be rectified. Rental providers must keep records of each check for five years and give the renter a copy within seven days. The deadline worth marking is 13 October 2026: from that date the two-yearly electrical and gas safety check obligation applies to all rental agreements, including those that began before the rules changed.
whenYouNeedIt: You are a rental provider and the property has not had an electrical safety check in the last two years
You own a Ballarat rental with an agreement that started before the rules changed - 13 October 2026 catches it
The property still has a ceramic fuse board or no safety switches
You manage multiple rentals and need checks scheduled and documented together
A renter has reported tripping circuits, a shock, or a fitting that gets hot

process.detail: The check needs access to the switchboard and every room with fixed wiring, so it is arranged with the renter rather than dropped on them.
Switchboard, fixed wiring, power points, hardwired light fittings and safety switches are assessed against section 4 of the periodic assessment standard.
Each safety switch is tested to confirm it trips within the required time. A visual check that one is fitted does not satisfy the requirement.
You get documentation for your five-year record and a copy for the renter within seven days, plus a quote for any rectification the check turns up.

subServices.priceGuide: A compliance check is generally quoted as a flat fee rather than hourly, and packaged checks across gas and smoke alarms usually price better than booking each separately. The variable is rectification: an older Ballarat rental that still has a fuse board will need a switchboard upgrade to comply, which is a separate job in the $735-$2,950 range plus the independent inspection fee. Ask for the check and any likely rectification to be quoted separately so you can see what compliance actually costs.

faqs.question: When does the two-yearly electrical safety check apply to my rental?
faqs.answer: From 13 October 2026 the mandatory two-yearly gas and electrical safety checks apply to all rental agreements in Victoria, whether the agreement started before, on or after that date. Rental providers must have the check done by a licensed electrician, keep records for five years, and give the renter a copy within seven days of each check.

faqs.question: Is checking that a safety switch is installed enough?
faqs.answer: No. Each installed RCD must be tested under load to confirm it trips within the required response time. A visual inspection confirming a safety switch is present does not meet the requirement - an RCD can be fitted and still fail to trip, which is precisely the failure mode the test exists to catch.

subServices.name: EV Charger Installation
subServices.blurb: Home wallbox installation for Ballarat EV owners - load assessment, dedicated circuit and compliant install. Compare quotes from local Registered Electrical Contractors.
subServices.whatItInvolves: Installing a home EV charger is a dedicated circuit job, not an outlet swap. A 7kW single-phase wallbox draws around 32 amps continuously for hours at a time, which is a heavier sustained load than almost anything else in a house, so the first step is assessing whether the existing switchboard and consumer mains can carry it alongside the rest of the home. Where they cannot, a switchboard upgrade or mains upgrade comes first. The install itself runs a dedicated correctly sized circuit from the board to the charger location with its own breaker and RCD protection of the type the charger requires, mounts and commissions the unit, and configures any load management or solar-diversion features so the charger throttles rather than tripping the main when the oven and heating are running. Cable route and length matter to the price - a charger on a wall next to the board is a very different job to one at the far end of a detached garage. In Victoria this is electrical installation work requiring a Certificate of Electrical Safety, and the distributor generally needs to be notified of the added load.
whenYouNeedIt: You have bought an EV or plug-in hybrid and are charging from a standard power point
Overnight charging from a 10A outlet is not returning enough range for your commute
You have rooftop solar and want the charger to soak up daytime excess
You are building or renovating in Lucas or Alfredton and want the circuit run before the walls close
The charger needs to go in a detached garage or carport away from the switchboard

process.detail: The electrician checks whether the switchboard, consumer mains and available capacity can carry a continuous 32A load on top of existing household demand.
Charger location, cable route and length are set - the biggest single variable in the price, especially to a detached garage.
A correctly sized dedicated circuit is run from the board with its own breaker and the RCD type the charger requires.
The wallbox is mounted, commissioned, load management or solar diversion configured, and a Certificate of Electrical Safety issued.

subServices.priceGuide: The two things that move an EV charger quote are the distance from the switchboard to the charger and whether the board can take the load as it stands. A short run next to an already-modern board is the cheap end; a long run to a detached garage, or a job that needs a switchboard or consumer mains upgrade first, is substantially more. Get the charger supply, the electrical install and any board upgrade itemised separately - some quotes bundle a unit you may not want.

faqs.question: Can I just charge from a normal power point?
faqs.answer: You can, using the portable cable most EVs ship with, but it is slow - a standard 10A outlet delivers roughly 10-15km of range per hour, so a meaningful top-up takes overnight and a full charge can take days. It also puts a sustained load through an outlet and circuit never designed for hours of continuous draw. A dedicated 7kW wallbox on its own circuit is both considerably faster and the safer arrangement for daily charging.

faqs.question: Will my switchboard handle an EV charger?
faqs.answer: Often not without work. A 7kW charger pulls around 32A continuously, which is a heavier sustained load than an oven or air conditioner, so an older board with limited spare capacity, no RCD protection, or undersized consumer mains usually needs upgrading first. A good installer assesses this before quoting rather than after starting - which is why quotes given over the phone without seeing the board are worth a second look.

subServices.name: House Rewiring & Old Wiring Repairs
subServices.blurb: Ballarat's older weatherboard and Victorian-era homes often still carry aged rubber or VIR wiring. Connect with electricians who test what is there and quote full or partial rewires.
subServices.whatItInvolves: Rewiring is the job Ballarat's housing stock generates more than most - a large share of the city's homes predate modern wiring standards, and the cabling installed in them has a service life. Rubber-insulated and VIR cable goes brittle and crumbles with age and heat, particularly in roof spaces, exposing conductors; early PVC hardens and cracks. The diagnostic step is insulation resistance testing, which measures whether the insulation between conductors and earth has degraded, and it gives a factual answer rather than an opinion about whether a rewire is genuinely needed. A full rewire replaces all circuit cabling, accessories and usually the switchboard, and is disruptive - cables are run through roof and subfloor spaces and walls where access allows, with some patching inevitable. A partial rewire replaces the worst circuits only, which is a legitimate staged approach where budget is the constraint. Older homes also commonly have too few circuits and too few outlets for how a house is actually used now, so a rewire is normally also the point at which circuits are properly split and outlets added.
whenYouNeedIt: The house still has cloth, rubber or VIR-insulated wiring, common in pre-1960s Ballarat homes
Insulation resistance testing has come back low on one or more circuits
Lights flicker or dim, or outlets and switches feel warm
You are renovating, and walls and ceilings are open anyway
There are too few power points and extension leads have become permanent fixtures

process.detail: Insulation resistance testing on each circuit establishes what has actually degraded, so the scope is based on measurement rather than the age of the house.
A staged partial rewire of the worst circuits is a legitimate option where a full rewire is out of budget - the electrician should price both.
New cabling is run through roof, subfloor and wall spaces, circuits properly split, and outlets added where the house has been running on extension leads.
The switchboard is generally replaced as part of the work, everything is tested, and certification issued - with independent inspection where the work is prescribed.

subServices.priceGuide: Rewiring is quoted per job, and the drivers are house size, number of circuits, and how accessible the roof and subfloor spaces are - a single-storey weatherboard with a walkable roof space is far cheaper to rewire than a double-storey with plaster ceilings and no access. Add the switchboard upgrade that normally accompanies it ($735-$2,950 plus $150-$300 inspection) and any plaster patching. Ask for a partial-rewire option priced alongside the full job; staging the work over time is common.

faqs.question: How do I know if my old Ballarat house actually needs rewiring?
faqs.answer: Age alone does not decide it - testing does. An electrician performs insulation resistance testing on each circuit to measure whether the insulation between conductors and earth has broken down. Visible signs worth acting on include cloth or rubber-sheathed cable in the roof space, brittle or crumbling insulation, warm outlets or switches, and repeated unexplained tripping. Any of those warrant a test rather than a wait.

faqs.question: Do I have to rewire the whole house at once?
faqs.answer: No. A partial rewire replacing only the circuits that fail testing is a common and legitimate staged approach, and it is often what is recommended where a full rewire is out of reach. The trade-off is that the remaining old circuits will need doing eventually and access work may be repeated, so ask for both options quoted so you can compare the staged cost against doing it once.

faqs.question: How much does an electrician cost in Ballarat?
faqs.answer: Victorian electricians typically charge $85-$130 per hour for standard residential work, plus a first-hour call-out fee generally in the $80-$150 range that usually covers travel and 30-60 minutes on site. Emergency and after-hours work runs higher, around $150-$250+ per hour. Common fixed jobs sit in known bands - a switchboard upgrade generally $735-$2,950, plus $150-$300 for the independent inspection prescribed work requires. Rates vary by contractor, so comparing two or three local quotes is worthwhile on anything beyond a minor callout.

faqs.question: Does electrical work in Victoria need a certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the Electricity Safety Act 1998 and the Electricity Safety (General) Regulations 2019, a Certificate of Electrical Safety must be issued for electrical installation work, completed by a Registered Electrical Contractor or licensed electrical worker, lodged electronically with Energy Safe Victoria, and a copy given to you. For prescribed work such as switchboard upgrades, a Licensed Electrical Inspector working independently of the contractor must also inspect the work and countersign the certificate. Always ask for your copy - it is your record that the work was done and certified.

faqs.question: What are the rules for rental properties in Victoria?
faqs.answer: Rental providers must have an electrical safety check of all switchboards, wiring and fittings carried out every two years by a licensed electrician, assessed against section 4 of AS/NZS 3019:2022. From 13 October 2026 this applies to all rental agreements, including those that began before the rules changed. Since 29 March 2023 rental properties have also required a modern-style switchboard with circuit breakers and safety switches. Each RCD must be tested under load, not just visually confirmed. Records must be kept for five years and the renter given a copy within seven days.

faqs.question: Is this an electrical contracting business?
faqs.answer: No. This site is a free quote-matching service for Ballarat households and rental providers. We are not electricians, we hold no REC registration or electrical licence, and we do not carry out work, issue Certificates of Electrical Safety or quote prices ourselves. You tell us the job and we connect you with local electricians who quote directly. Always confirm a contractor's REC registration, licence and insurance with them before work starts.
